premise: A monster sinks a cargo ship in the opening; the survivor's home keeps breaking and shrinking as he tries to reach an island surrounded by dangerous reefs.
cast: Marin: navy cap always retained, yellow vest, white round head/white hands/feet, thin black limbs.
Tess: adult deckhand in coral safety vest over dark simplified clothing; white circular head/hands/feet; one crew card.
locations: Opening cargo emergency ladder -> detached raft.
Cargo-debris field -> storm-damaged raft -> outer island reef.
First failed rock passage -> observed inlet beside hooked rock -> sheltered beach/shade.
chronology: Days1-3: ship sinks immediately, bag freed, Tess rescued, lid/tarp recovered.
Days5-11: padded frame/canopy, disturbances observed, paddle lost to shark, rain collected.
Days14-20: island sighted, storm tears tarp/bends rod/loses crate; tube repaired and pumped.
Days21-25: first reef approach damages remaining paddle; kept cooler lid tested as steering surface.
Days26-29: shared practice, shark return, wrong wind postpones approach, crew-card conversation.
Day30: observed creature turn, reef crossing, lid released at snag, landing and raft secured.
setups_and_payoffs: Saving bag and Tess in hook pays off through shared supplies/crew-card ending.
Paddle loss and failed approach lead to practice with already retained lid.
Observed monster movement and shallower passage permit escape without killing beast or surprise rescue.
persistent_states: Cargo ship never reappears and is never reclaimed.
Supply bag freed before line cut; Tess rescued with released line; crew card planted at ladder.
Cooler lid stays aboard throughout; no miraculous reappearance of a lost prop.
First paddle blade gone; second blade loses corner but remains usable; broken piece retained.
Crate abandoned in storm; rod bent/inactive among damaged raft gear; tarp torn but usable scrap remains.
Patch is temporary; hand pump used repeatedly; no miracle permanent repair.
No chart exists, no late magic mirror distraction, no exact tide timetable or real-world survival advice.
Signature cap not borrowed away; beach is distinct from prior fishing-boat/buoy-rescue pilot.
visual_reference_status: Use existing preset main/drawing guide; prepare and inspect recurring side-character and new-location references before scenes.
